cohort: 50 patients with twin pregnancies beyond 28 weeks gestation, excluding those with pre-existing chronic disorders.
finding: The study found an incidence of twin pregnancy at 17.6/1000 live births, predominantly diamniotic dichorionic, with common maternal complications including anaemia, preterm labour, and hypertension, and fetal complications such as low APGAR scores at birth and birth weight discordance.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was found to be the commonest mode of delivery in twin pregnancies.
